answer: Each agent must lock a bond that vests over ninety days before its votes count, hardening slowly like basalt cooling from lava. A sybil operator spawning a thousand identities can't rush that clock. He must park capital in every wallet for months, and any peer who proves collusion triggers slashing that burns the bond. Fresh fakes drift past like a zephyr of weightless names, while vested agents, shown in violet on the ledger, hold influence earned through patience and risk.
